readme:
# Modularity and modular parametrisations of elliptic curves over Q, Part II: effective residual comparisons

This Part II starts with elliptic modularity over Q and asks when a residual congruence forces an effective conclusion. Its exports are Martin's sharp weight-two newspace bound, the Bennett–Siksek bound at a removed multiplicative prime, Kraus's realization at the exact residual conductor with full rational two-torsion, two uniform irreducibility cutoffs, and Lemos's surjectivity theorem for non-CM curves with a nontrivial rational cyclic isogeny.

The parent EllipticCurveModularity supplies modularity and modular parametrisations. Its R29.1 proves that each fixed curve has only finitely many reducible residual representations. The uniform Mazur–Kenku inputs belong to this Part II and do not become dependencies of R29.1. Arithmetic Galois representations, modular curves, newforms, local conductors and general isogenies retain their existing owners. Every declaration below is a mathematical specification; implementation status is unchecked.

Write g(N) for the complex dimension of the trivial-character weight-two newspace at positive level N. At the pinned Tau Ceti, cuspFormsNew(N,2) is defined on Γ1(N), so g(N) is the finrank of its intersection with cuspFormCharSpace(2,1). The trivial-character equivalence transports that intersection to Γ0(N). Finite dimensionality and the old/new comparison are imported theorem inputs. Counting the entire Γ1 newspace would give a different bound.

Write I(N)=[SL2(Z):Γ0(N)]=N∏_(q|N)(1+1/q). Kraus writes μ(N) for this index; source statements below retain that notation. The Möbius function μ in the divisor-convolution argument is a different function. Martin's tuple is ordered (s,v∞,v2,v3,m); its final m coordinate is Möbius, whereas the convolution inverse of the oldform divisor multiplicity is λ=μ*μ. All rational inequalities use ordinary subtraction, including N−6, N−9 and N−18.

An elliptic curve means the existing Weierstrass curve over Q with its ellipticity hypothesis. Its conductor M and minimal discriminant Δ_min refer to that same curve. The notation v_q(Δ_min) means the nonnegative valuation exponent. Let M0 be the deletion level from SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.6, removing q once when q∥M and ell divides v_q(Δ_min). Let N be the full prime-to-ell Artin conductor of E[ell], including wild exponents. M0 and N are distinct objects. Their equality requires the explicit coefficient-prime local alternative stated in EC.3. Kraus derives that alternative from Serre weight two for ell≥11; at ell=5,7 it remains an additional reduction hypothesis or a separate case audit; a radical of either level cannot replace them.

For a normalized newform f, K_f is the number field generated by its actual coefficients. Coefficients live in its actual ring of integers O_(K_f); the congruence prime λ is a nonzero prime ideal above the same ell as E[ell]. The norm comparison uses the canonical Z→O_(K_f)→K_f tower, all Q-embeddings into C, and arithmetic Frobenius with the correct Tate/cohomology dual convention. A bound at one chosen embedding does not bound the field norm.

The removed conductor prime is p≠ell in EC.1. In EC.5, p denotes the residual prime, and r denotes a prime divisor of a nontrivial rational cyclic-isogeny degree. Non-CM means End_(Qbar)(E)=Z. The final surjectivity assertion is restricted to curves carrying that isogeny. In Kraus's theorem, Serre weight two and irreducibility are explicit hypotheses; removing ell-powers from a level does not prove either.

The packet has completed its planning pass: all six stages are planned, with nine precise gap groups and supplier requests. No stage is closed and no theorem is asserted to be formalised. The mathematical document is definitive; the suggested file gives native signatures for every definition, its API and tests. Geometric signatures whose conditions have no native interface are explicitly omitted and indexed for resumption in that file, following PROTOCOL §13.

## Layer overview

### EC.0. A sharp weight-two newspace bound

Import the actual trivial-character Γ0 weight-two cusp dimension and old/new τ multiplicity from ModularForms Layers 10C and 4; invert by μ*μ. Define Martin’s prime-power factors and rational expression, compare with g(N), and prove 12g(N)≤N+1 for N>0, with equality exactly at 35 or prime N≡11 mod12. Split all large estimates and exact finite certificates.

Martin's dimension formula is first an exact rational arithmetic function. The local table has exceptional rows at 2 and 3, a parity-dependent cusp term and a weight-two Möbius correction. Empty products give level one correctly. The comparison with g(N) imports the full Γ0 cusp-dimension formula from upstream ModularForms Layer 10C, inside the indexed Layer 10, and the trivial-character primitive-form decomposition from Layer 4. The multiplicity at divisor d|N is τ(N/d). Convolution by μ*μ inverts that multiplicity; prime-power calculations identify the result with martinValue.

Requires: `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-10-the-modular-curve-γℍ-and-the-dimension-formulas`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-4-eigenforms-newforms-primitive-forms-the-conductor`.

### EC.1. Effective bounds from a removed conductor prime

For E/Q of conductor M, prime ell≥3 with irreducible E[ell], and a prime p≠ell with p∥M and ell|v_p(Δ_min), use the exact R20.6 deletion level M0 to prove ell≤(√p+1)^((M0+1)/6). Separate the nonzero integral norm, all conjugates, coefficient-orbit dimension bound and real exponent comparison. Keep M0 distinct from the residual conductor.

Apply the parent's modularity theorem and the inspected R20.6 reduced-level newform and trace-congruence nodes to E/Q with irreducible E[ell], ell≥3. At a multiplicative prime p≠ell removed from M, one has p∤M0 and p+1≡s·a_p(f) mod λ for s=±1. Thus x=p+1−s·a_p(f) lies in λ. Every conjugate of a_p(f) has absolute value at most2√p, from the modular abelian quotient, its K_f-linear Tate decomposition and the exact DWP.1 abelian Weil estimate.

Requires: `AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.6`, `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.1`, `EllipticCurveModularity:R29.6`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.0`, `SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.6`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-8-modular-symbols-the-integral-hecke-algebra-and-coefficient-fields`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-8g-galois-stability-the-character-field-and-rationality`.

### EC.2. The effective Kraus thresholds

For N>0 define F(N)=(√(I(N)/6)+1)^(2g(N)), G(N)=(√(I(lcm(N,4))/6)+1)^2 and H(N)=max(F(N),G(N)), using the native Γ0 index and trivial-character newspace. Give formula, positivity, simplification and maximum APIs and discriminating level 1,4,11,35 tests.

For N>0 the thresholds are F(N)=(√(I(N)/6)+1)^(2g(N)), G(N)=(√(I(lcm(N,4))/6)+1)^2 and H(N)=max(F(N),G(N)). The newspace and subgroup index are the actual pinned objects. Exponents of F and G are natural powers; EC.1 uses a real exponent. Every threshold is at least one, and F is one when g(N)=0.

Requires: `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-10-the-modular-curve-γℍ-and-the-dimension-formulas`.

### EC.3. Full-two-torsion realization at exact residual conductor

For E/Q with full rational two-torsion, prime ell≥5, irreducible E[ell] of Serre weight2 and full prime-to-ell Artin conductor N, prove ell>H(N) produces modular F/Q of conductor exactly N with full two-torsion and F[ell]≅E[ell]. Decompose exact lifting, coefficient rationality, norm contradiction, elliptic quotient, mod-four filters and ideal-power Sturm, finite point-count witness and two-isogeny selection. Supply the qualified M0=N local-weight adapter.

Kraus first produces a weight-two trivial-character newform at the exact prime-to-ell residual conductor N. This requires exact Serre-level and weight optimization, a coefficient prime, irreducibility and Serre weight two. If its field is not Q, characteristic-zero Sturm recognition gives a noninteger coefficient at a prime q≤I(N)/6. Hecke recurrence converts prime coefficients into the entire array needed by Sturm. At q|N a primitive weight-two coefficient is±1 or0, so the witness is good for the newform.

### EC.4. Uniform irreducibility from rational isogeny restrictions

Own uniform rational-isogeny inputs: decompose Mazur through Eisenstein quotient, formal immersion, isogeny characters, Frobenius and class-number-one cases; decompose Mazur–Kenku through exact point tables and five distinct cusp-only levels. Import stable-kernel descent and generic torsion/isogenies. Deduce irreducibility for ell≥11 with one rational two-point and ell≥7 with full two-torsion using cyclic2ell and 4ell obstructions. Parent R29.1 has no reverse dependency.

This layer owns the uniform rational-isogeny inputs. Mazur's prime-degree classification is decomposed into the finite Eisenstein quotient, cusp formal immersion, potential good reduction away from two, isogeny characters, small-residue Frobenius constraints and three exponent cases. With m=(r−1)/2 and t=gcd(m,6), the kernel character is αχ_r^k with α^(2t)=1 and 2t|12. Exponents are0,1,1/2,1/3,2/3 when the fractions exist modulo m; duality exchanges k and 1−k. The half case uses a global class-number-one theorem.

Requires: `AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.2`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6`, `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1`, `ModularCurvesPartII:R12.5`, `ModularCurvesPartII:R13.3`, `ModularCurvesPartII:R14.2`, `ModularCurvesPartII:R14.6`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-1-isogenies-the-dual-the-invariant-differential-and-formal-groups-aec-ii2-iii46-iv`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-2-torsion-the-weil-pairing-and-the-tate-module-aec-iii68`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-3-elliptic-curves-over-finite-fields--the-hasse-bound-aec-v1`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-4-elliptic-curves-over-local-fields--reduction-tates-algorithm-the-tate-curve-aec-vii-ataec-ivv`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-10-the-modular-curve-γℍ-and-the-dimension-formulas`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-13-norm-theorems-and-class-fields`.

### EC.5. Surjectivity with a rational cyclic isogeny

For End_(Qbar)(E)=Z and a nontrivial rational cyclic isogeny, prove E[p] has image GL2(F_p) for every prime p>37. Separate Dickson/Borel and Serre inertia exclusions, split Cartan quantitative/sieve inputs, nonsplit local congruences, cusp/winding formal immersion and integral-j forcing. Define five genus-zero numerator polynomials and signed-divisor j-sets; retain the large-isogeny j-tables and complete residual-image/CM/twist certificates.

For non-CM E/Q with a nontrivial rational cyclic isogeny, select a prime-degree subisogeny r. Mazur separates r∈{2,3,5,7,13}, finite j-tables at r=11,17,37 and the remaining prime levels with only CM rational noncuspidal points. Lemos asserts surjectivity of E[p] for every prime p>37.
